all.name: Detect things in the text of the terminals
all.what: Heidrun Code reads the text of every terminal to find web addresses, references to issues and commits, file paths, commands, and more. This switch turns all of this detection on or off.
all.on: Each family below follows its own switch. Heidrun Code colors the text it finds, shows hover buttons near it, and runs an action when you click a button or ⌘-click the text.
all.off: Heidrun Code colors nothing, shows no hover button, and gives no action to the text of any terminal. It also reads no question and no numbered choice from the agents. The text of the terminal is never changed in either case.
family.webAddresses.name: Web addresses
family.webAddresses.what: Web addresses that start with http:// or https:// in the text of a terminal.
family.webAddresses.on: The address is underlined while the pointer is over it. A ⌘-click opens it in the browser.
family.webAddresses.off: A web address is plain text. A ⌘-click does nothing, unless the address is an issue, a pull request, a merge request, or a commit and the family of that kind is on.
family.issueReferences.name: Issues
family.issueReferences.what: References to the issues of the code hosting service of the workspace.
family.issueReferences.on: The reference is colored, and underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the buttons “Open” and “Preview”. A ⌘-click shows the preview in Heidrun Code. The workspace needs a Git remote for the destination: without it the reference is colored and has no action.
family.issueReferences.off: The references to issues have no color, no underline, no button, and no action.
family.requestReferences.name: Pull requests and merge requests
family.requestReferences.what: References to the pull requests of GitHub and the merge requests of GitLab.
family.requestReferences.on: The reference is colored, and underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the buttons “Open” and “Preview”. A ⌘-click shows the preview in Heidrun Code.
family.requestReferences.off: The references to pull requests and merge requests have no color, no underline, no button, and no action. A number written as #12 after the words “PR” or “pull request” is not read as an issue instead.
family.tickets.name: Ticket keys (ABC-123)
family.tickets.what: Keys of the ticket tracker of the project, for example ABC-123.
family.tickets.on: The key is colored, and underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the button “Open”, which opens the ticket in the browser.
family.tickets.off: The ticket keys have no color, no underline, no button, and no action.
family.commits.name: Commits
family.commits.on: The identifier is colored, and underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the button “Open”, which opens the commit in the browser. The workspace needs a Git remote for the destination.
family.commits.off: The commit identifiers have no color, no underline, no button, and no action.
family.filePaths.name: File paths
family.filePaths.what: Paths of files that an agent or a program writes in the terminal.
family.filePaths.on: The path is underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the button “Open”, and a ⌘-click does the same. A relative path starts at the folder of the pane. The file opens in the File explorer sidebar section.
family.filePaths.off: The file paths have no underline, no button, and no action.
family.shellCommands.name: Shell commands
family.shellCommands.what: Commands that a coding agent suggests with an exclamation mark.
family.shellCommands.on: The command is underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the button “Run”. A click types the command in the input of the coding agent with the exclamation mark and sends it. The guards check the command first.
family.shellCommands.off: The suggested commands have no underline, no button, and no action. The line stays as it is, and the other pieces of the line stay unreachable.
family.slashCommands.name: Slash commands
family.slashCommands.what: Slash commands of Claude Code, such as /compact.
family.slashCommands.on: The command is underlined under the pointer. The pointer shows the button “Run”. A click sends the command to Claude Code.
family.slashCommands.off: The slash commands have no underline, no button, and no action.
family.numberedSteps.name: Numbered steps
family.numberedSteps.what: The items of a numbered list that a coding agent writes.
family.numberedSteps.on: The pointer shows the button “Do step”. A click sends a message to the coding agent that asks it to do this step.
family.numberedSteps.off: The numbered items have no button and no action.
family.agentList.name: Agent list and input box
family.agentList.what: The list of agents that Claude Code shows under its input, and the input box.
family.agentList.on: The pointer shows the button “Show” on a row. A click shows that agent without the arrow keys. A click in the input box, while a row has the selection, gives the keyboard back to the input.
family.agentList.off: The rows of the list and the input box have no button and no action. The arrow keys still work.
family.questionsAndChoices.name: Questions and numbered choices
family.questionsAndChoices.what: The question that ends the last message of a coding agent, and the numbered menu of an agent that waits for you.
family.questionsAndChoices.on: The Needs you sidebar section shows the question and the buttons of the menu, and the phone shows them too.
family.questionsAndChoices.off: The Needs you sidebar section shows no question and no button for a menu. The agent still waits in its pane.
sample.name: Try a text
sample.what: Type or paste a text to see what Heidrun Code finds in it. Nothing is opened, sent, or run.
sample.how: Each line of the text is read like a line of a terminal, with the repository of the selected workspace and the kind of pane that you choose. The result shows what was found and where, the destination, the hover buttons, and which rule took the text when two rules found it. A family that is off is shown as off.
sample.noRepository: The selected workspace has no known repository. Issues and commits are colored, and have no destination.
sample.nothing: Nothing is found in this text.
sample.isOff: This family is off: nothing happens for this text.
sample.noAction: Found, but with no destination: the text is colored and has no action.
sample.suppressed: “{text}” also matches {family} ({rule}), but {winnerFamily} ({winnerRule}) takes this text first.
sample.question: Question found: {question}
action.openAddress: opens the address in the browser
action.previewIssue: shows the issue or the request in the preview window
action.openFile: opens the file in the File explorer
action.sendPrompt: types the text in the input of the coding agent and sends it
action.backToPrompt: gives the keyboard back to the input
intro: Heidrun Code reads the text on the screen of each terminal and offers a button for what it recognizes. It never changes the text. This page lists every rule with its exact pattern and with examples. Each example was run through the real detection, in the project of the selected workspace.
project.title: Project of the selected workspace
project.noWorkspace: No workspace is selected, so the examples run without a repository.
project.referencesSwitch: References switched on in the project
project.anyPrefix: any, except the words UTF, ISO, SHA, RFC, and a few more
project.off: no: the key enabled of references is false in .heidrun/config.json
project.configHint: Heidrun Code reads the repository from the Git remote of the folder of the workspace. The key references of the file .heidrun/config.json of the project can replace it, and sets the ticket address.
pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.pathGithub: The path of the address must end like this on GitHub
pattern.pathGitlab: The path of the address must end like this on GitLab
pattern.pathGithubForm: Address without its host, in the form of GitHub
pattern.pathGitlabForm: Address without its host, in the form of GitLab
pattern.commitPathGithub: The path of the address of a commit on GitHub
pattern.commitPathGitlab: The path of the address of a commit on GitLab
pattern.boxRule: A line that closes the input box
pattern.agentRow: A row of the agent list
pattern.option: A numbered option of the menu
ruleWhat.address: A web address: http or https, two slashes, then the characters of the address. A full stop, a comma, a colon, an exclamation mark, or a question mark at the end is not part of it.
ruleWhat.fullAddress: The whole web address of an issue, a pull request, or a merge request. On GitHub: …/issues/N or …/pull/N, on github.com or on the host of the repository. On GitLab: …/-/issues/N or …/-/merge_requests/N, on any host except github.com.
ruleWhat.pathAddress: The same address written without its host. It goes to the repository of the pane, or to the repository that the text names. A leading slash, or a repository in front, is required.
ruleWhat.crossRepository: The path of another repository, then # for an issue or ! for a merge request, then the number.
ruleWhat.hash: A number sign and a number, not after a letter, a digit, &, #, or /. It goes to the repository of the pane.
ruleWhat.explicit: The words PR, MR, pull request, or merge request, then a number, with # or ! allowed before it. It goes to the repository of the pane.
ruleWhat.bang: An exclamation mark and a number, not after a letter or a digit. It is the merge request of GitLab: in a GitHub project nothing is found.
ruleWhat.ticket: Two to ten capital letters or digits that start with a letter, a hyphen, and a number. It needs a ticket address in the project. Words such as UTF-8 are not tickets, unless the project lists their prefix.
ruleWhat.commitAddress: The whole web address of a commit: …/commit/<identifier> on GitHub, …/-/commit/<identifier> on GitLab.
ruleWhat.commitHash: 7 to 40 characters from 0 to 9 and a to f, with at least one letter and one digit, and not inside a longer word.
ruleWhat.filePath: Folders and a file name with an extension, and an optional line and column. A bare file name needs a line number. A full stop followed by a letter never ends the path.
ruleWhat.inlineShell: An exclamation mark, a space, and a command inside a sentence. The first word must be a path, a script, or a known tool, so “Super ! Bravo” is not a command. The sentence is read on all the lines that the coding agent wrapped, so a long command is sent whole, on one line.
ruleWhat.shellBlock: A line that starts with an exclamation mark and a command. The command goes on over the lines that the coding agent wrapped, and over the lines after a line that ends with \, &&, ||, |, or ;. It is sent on one line, and shown under the button before the click.
ruleWhat.slashCommand: A slash and the name of a command that Claude Code knows in the folder of the pane. The word must not touch another slash or a path.
ruleWhat.numberedStep: A number of one or two digits, a full stop or a closing parenthesis, a space, and at least 4 characters.
ruleWhat.promptBox: The input box of Claude Code, when a row of the agent list has the selection. A click in the box gives the keyboard back to the input.
ruleWhat.agentRow: A row of the agent list under the input box: a marker (● or ○) and the name of an agent. At least two rows together, near the bottom of the screen.
ruleWhat.question: The last paragraph of the last message of the agent, when it ends with a question mark in its last three lines.
ruleWhat.choices: A menu of numbered options that starts at 1, has exactly one selected option (❯), and is the last thing on the screen.
pane.agent: Panes that run a coding agent
need.repository: This project has no repository: the text is found, but it has no destination.
need.ticketAddress: This project has no ticket address: nothing is found.
need.gitlab: This project is not on GitLab: nothing is found.
need.knownCommands: No slash command is known in this project: nothing is found.
